text: What are the two main types of debentures?
options: Convertible Debentures, Non-Convertible Debentures
Redeemable Debentures, Irredeemable Debentures
Secured Debentures, Unsecured Debentures
Fixed Rate Debentures, Floating Rate Debentures
explanation: According to NCERT, debentures can be classified into two main types: Convertible Debentures and Non-Convertible Debentures. Convertible Debentures can be converted into shares of the company at a predetermined future date, while Non-Convertible Debentures cannot be converted into shares.
subject: Accountancy
chapter: Ch 7: Issue and Redemption of Debentures

text: What is the main purpose of issuing debentures as collateral security?
options: To raise long-term funds
To reduce the cost of capital
To provide collateral security to debenture holders
To increase the number of shareholders
correctAnswer: To provide collateral security to debenture holders
explanation: According to NCERT, debentures can be issued as collateral security to provide security to debenture holders. This is done to ensure that the company can repay the debenture holders in case of default.
subject: Accountancy
chapter: Ch 7: Issue and Redemption of Debentures

text: What is the accounting treatment for writing off discount/loss on issue of debentures?
options: Debit Discount on Issue of Debentures, Credit Cash
Debit Cash, Credit Discount on Issue of Debentures
Debit Loss on Issue of Debentures, Credit Discount on Issue of Debentures
Debit Discount on Issue of Debentures, Credit Loss on Issue of Debentures
correctAnswer: Debit Discount on Issue of Debentures, Credit Cash
explanation: According to NCERT, when a company issues debentures at a discount, the discount is written off by debiting Discount on Issue of Debentures and crediting Cash.
subject: Accountancy
chapter: Ch 7: Issue and Redemption of Debentures

text: What is the difference between a redeemable debenture and an irredeemable debenture?
options: Redeemable debenture can be redeemed at face value, while irredeemable debenture cannot be redeemed
Redeemable debenture can be redeemed at a premium, while irredeemable debenture cannot be redeemed
Redeemable debenture can be redeemed at a discount, while irredeemable debenture cannot be redeemed
Redeemable debenture can be redeemed at a premium or discount, while irredeemable debenture cannot be redeemed
correctAnswer: Redeemable debenture can be redeemed at face value, while irredeemable debenture cannot be redeemed
explanation: According to NCERT, a redeemable debenture can be redeemed at face value, while an irredeemable debenture cannot be redeemed.
subject: Accountancy
chapter: Ch 7: Issue and Redemption of Debentures

text: What is the accounting treatment for redemption of debentures?
options: Debit Debenture Redemption Reserve, Credit Debentures
Debit Debentures, Credit Debenture Redemption Reserve
Debit Cash, Credit Debentures
Debit Debentures, Credit Cash
correctAnswer: Debit Debenture Redemption Reserve, Credit Debentures
explanation: According to NCERT, when a company redeems debentures, the debenture redemption reserve is debited and debentures are credited.
subject: Accountancy
chapter: Ch 7: Issue and Redemption of Debentures

text: What is the difference between a secured debenture and an unsecured debenture?
options: Secured debenture is backed by collateral, while unsecured debenture is not backed by collateral
Secured debenture is not backed by collateral, while unsecured debenture is backed by collateral
Secured debenture is issued at a premium, while unsecured debenture is issued at a discount
Secured debenture is issued at a discount, while unsecured debenture is issued at a premium
correctAnswer: Secured debenture is backed by collateral, while unsecured debenture is not backed by collateral
explanation: According to NCERT, a secured debenture is backed by collateral, while an unsecured debenture is not backed by collateral.
subject: Accountancy
chapter: Ch 7: Issue and Redemption of Debentures

text: What is the accounting treatment for issue of debentures at a premium?
options: Debit Premium on Issue of Debentures, Credit Cash
Debit Cash, Credit Premium on Issue of Debentures
Debit Premium on Issue of Debentures, Credit Debentures
Debit Debentures, Credit Premium on Issue of Debentures
correctAnswer: Debit Premium on Issue of Debentures, Credit Cash
explanation: According to NCERT, when a company issues debentures at a premium, the premium is debited and cash is credited.

text: What is the difference between a fixed rate debenture and a floating rate debenture?
options: Fixed rate debenture has a fixed rate of interest, while floating rate debenture has a floating rate of interest
Fixed rate debenture has a floating rate of interest, while floating rate debenture has a fixed rate of interest
Fixed rate debenture is issued at a premium, while floating rate debenture is issued at a discount
Fixed rate debenture is issued at a discount, while floating rate debenture is issued at a premium
correctAnswer: Fixed rate debenture has a fixed rate of interest, while floating rate debenture has a floating rate of interest
explanation: According to NCERT, a fixed rate debenture has a fixed rate of interest, while a floating rate debenture has a floating rate of interest.

Debit Debentures, Credit Cash
